name: The Royale Restaurant (Ojaswi Resort)
signature_dish: kumaoni thali with bhatt ki churkani
why_it_matters: Ojaswi is the #1-ranked resort in Chaukori on TripAdvisor and its Royale Restaurant is the village's only proper multi-cuisine kitchen with a Kumaoni section — bhatt ki churkani, aloo ke gutke, madua roti made by local cooks. The dining room faces the Panchachuli range head-on.
insider_tip: Ask the kitchen for the Kumaoni thali instead of the standard menu — it's prepared on request and is what the local staff eat. Non-residents need to call ahead (+91 89294 60558); the dining room prioritises in-house guests in season.
signature_address: Tea Garden, near Police Chauki, Chaukori, Pithoragarh 262531, Uttarakhand

name: KMVN Tourist Rest House Restaurant
why_it_matters: The Kumaon Mandal Vikas Nigam (Uttarakhand state tourism) rest house — Chaukori's oldest formal accommodation, sitting on the highest point of the ridge. Buffet breakfast comes with the room; non-residents are usually accommodated for lunch and dinner if you walk in early.
insider_tip: Menu lists more than the kitchen carries — confirm what's actually available before ordering. The aloo paratha breakfast is the consistent win; avoid Chinese items, they're an afterthought.
signature_address: KMVN TRH, Chaukori, Pithoragarh District 262531, Uttarakhand

name: Gud Chah Cafe & Restaurant
signature_dish: Kumaoni high tea with madua biscuits
why_it_matters: The only standalone cafe in Chaukori not attached to a resort — a small homestay-cafe combo whose name means 'good tea' in Kumaoni. Rooftop terrace with Panchachuli views, lunch + dinner + high tea, vegetarian-leaning menu.
insider_tip: Walk up at 4pm for high tea on the rooftop — that's their best hour, with the snow line catching the light. Skip the elaborate Chinese; stick to the Kumaoni thali and the chai.
signature_address: Gud Chah Cafe & Restaurant, Chaukori 262531, Pithoragarh District, Uttarakhand

name: Neelgagan Resort Restaurant
why_it_matters: Neelgagan is one of three Booking.com-listed resorts in Chaukori with a real in-house restaurant — a single dining hall serving residents plus drop-ins. Menu is limited and reviews call the food 'average'; this is utility dining for travellers stuck without options after dark.
insider_tip: Eat early — dinner service stops by 9.30pm sharp because the kitchen closes when the last in-house guest finishes. The garden seating is the reason to come; the food itself is workmanlike.
signature_address: Neelgagan Resort, Chaukori 262531, Pithoragarh District, Uttarakhand

name: Misty Mountains Retreat (Jhaltola)
signature_dish: Pahari home-cooked thali with organic estate produce
why_it_matters: Set on a 1,000-acre forest estate at Jhaltola village (~20km from Chaukori, near Patal Bhuvneshwar) — boutique retreat where dining is integrated into the stay: open dining hall, home-style Pahari cooking, organic produce from the estate, homemade jams and pickles. Outsider lunches by prior arrangement only.
insider_tip: Not a walk-in restaurant — call ahead for day-visit lunch (₹1000-1500 set menu). Combine with a Patal Bhuvneshwar cave visit since both sit on the same ridge road.
signature_address: Jhaltola Estate, near Chaukori and Patal Bhuvneshwar, Gangolihat, Pithoragarh, Uttarakhand
